geometry.locator: centroids of OSM way/171900951, way/171900954, way/171900955, way/171900956 as of the 2026-10-25T10:35:43Z OSM API extract; H.E.S.S. Telescopes page 'Arrangement of the telescopes'
geometry.note: 'Derived' rather than 'verified': the shape is computed from four telescope positions, so it stays derived even though its perimeter check passes.
geometry.quote: The initial four H.E.S.S. telescopes (Phase I) are arranged in form of a square with 120 m side length ... The diagonal of the square is oriented north-south.

method: Quadrilateral whose four vertices are the centroids (hepgraph.atlas.geo.centroid) of the four corner-telescope footprints, OpenStreetMap ways 171900951 (north), 171900954 (east), 171900955 (south), 171900956 (west), joined N-E-S-W. Replaces the previous square, which had been placed on the array's published coordinate and so carried that coordinate's 200 m uncertainty. The perimeter check compares this OSM-derived quadrilateral with the published 120 m side (480 m perimeter): an independent test, because the OSM positions were not fitted to it.
name: H.E.S.S. CT1-CT4 telescope square (120 m side, diagonal north-south)
notes: The vertices are telescope centres traced by OpenStreetMap mappers; the polygon is the geometric outline of the four telescope positions, not a structure on the ground.

summary.plain: The square formed by H.E.S.S.'s original four 12-metre telescopes, 120 metres to a side, with a north-south diagonal.
